dek: Lucy Vives's debut EP is five songs, 14 minutes, and entirely her own voice.

slides.label: The Name
slides.text: Her last name is Vives, but this project is *hers*: five songs she co-wrote, in an indie, alt pop lane.

slides.label: Who She Is
slides.text: Real name *Lucía Vives Gómez*. She's 30, daughter of Carlos Vives and Herlinda Gómez.

slides.label: Hometown
slides.text: Born in *San Germán, Puerto Rico*, she grew up moving between Puerto Rico, Colombia and the U.S.

slides.label: First Steps
slides.text: 2021: she joined her father and Mau y Ricky on *"Besos en Cualquier Horario,"* No. 10 on Latin Pop Airplay.

slides.label: Solo Debut
slides.text: 2022: her solo debut *"Cenizas."* Then she went quiet for *nearly four years*.

slides.label: The Comeback
slides.text: April 2026: she returned with *"Mascacielo,"* a comeback single with a video she directed herself.

slides.label: cimiento
slides.text: November 5, 2026: she released *cimiento*, her debut EP, five songs she calls *"a beginning."*

slides.label: What's Next
slides.text: Billboard just named her one of its emerging Latin artists to watch. *No tour dates* yet, more music promised.

caption_instagram:
Lucy Vives cimiento is her first EP, and the name Vives only gets her in the door.

Born in San Germán, Puerto Rico, raised between the island, Colombia and the U.S., Lucía Vives Gómez spent years building toward this: "Besos en Cualquier Horario" with her father and Mau y Ricky in 2021, her solo debut "Cenizas" in 2022, then nearly four years of quiet before "Mascacielo" brought her back.

Five songs, about 14 minutes, all co-written by her, and Billboard already has her on its emerging Latin artists to watch list.

Which cimiento track are you adding to your playlist: Mascacielo, Nido or Palpita?

caption_linkedin:
Lucy Vives just released cimiento, her debut EP, five songs she co-wrote herself. Her father is Carlos Vives. This project is not.

The build took years: a 2021 feature with her father and Mau y Ricky, a solo debut in 2022, then nearly four years of quiet before she came back this year with "Mascacielo," a video she directed herself, and two more singles that led into the EP.

That's the part worth sitting with. A recognizable last name can open a door, but it does not write the songs, direct the video or fill four quiet years with the work that makes a comeback land. Billboard just named her one of its emerging Latin artists to watch, on her own terms.
